- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 1–2% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30), model tends to underestimate downward moves — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent price is falling.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.30), model often overestimates upside — cap forecast at 1–2% below prior 30-day high or use 10-day SMA for anchoring.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for first 3–5 days if sentiment swings >0.30.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true price, especially if price is trending down.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model often overestimates mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is negative and price is above 30-day SMA.
- If sentiment is positive and price is below 30-day SMA, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid “overbought” bias.
